summary: Design panel: vet MATLAB implementation of the 5 hard chirp-analysis components against the spec anti-bias rules

designs.component: TFR + ridge extraction: chirp_tfr_faslt.m (FASLT power TFR 20-70 Hz) and chirp_ridge.m (tfridge ridge tracking on 25-58 Hz with iterative surrogate-gated peeling, transition-window derivation, ridge-power-dip statistic, and subject-average f_hi/f_lo anchors)
designs.functionSignature: function tfr = chirp_tfr_faslt(epochs, fs, cfg)  % and  function R = chirp_ridge(tfr, cfg)  -- where cfg may be shared; anchors via function A = chirp_ridge_anchors(meanTFR, tfr.freqs, cfg)
steps: chirp_tfr_faslt INPUTS: epochs = [nSamp x nTrial] real broadband signal (already epoched [-1,+3]s around finalOnset WITH extra filter/TFR pad beyond, demeaned/detrended per epoch upstream in 6.1); fs=500; cfg fields flo=20, fhi=70, df<=1 (so Nf = round((fhi-flo)/df)+1 ~= 51 at 1 Hz), c1=3, olo=3, ohi=30, mult=1, trimSamp = pad samples to strip off each end after transform.

chirp_tfr_faslt KERNEL CACHE: nfaslt rebuilds the wavelet bank on every call, which is the per-trial cost. Build the bank ONCE per channel: persistent/cached struct keyed on (fs,flo,fhi,Nf,c1,olo,ohi,mult). Either (a) precompute the cxmorlet set with the same linspace(flo,fhi,Nf) + ceil(linspace(olo,ohi,Nf)) order schedule that nfaslt uses and convolve directly, or (b) wrap nfaslt but memoize the `wavelets` cell + `padding` across trials. Spec 6.2 mandates caching across trials within a channel; do NOT call vanilla nfaslt in the trial loop without caching.

chirp_tfr_faslt TRANSFORM: for each trial column, wt = nfaslt(sig', fs, [flo fhi], Nf, c1, [olo ohi], mult) giving POWER [Nf x nSamp] (magnitude^2, geometric-mean pooled across superlet orders -- it is NOT analytic; never derive phase/envelope from it, per KEY API FACT). Stack into P [Nf x nSamp x nTrial]. Trim the pad: P = P(:, trimSamp+1:end-trimSamp, :). Build time vector t relative to finalOnset (0 = onset).

chirp_tfr_faslt OUTPUTS struct tfr: .power [Nf x nT x nTrial], .meanPower = mean over trials (power-averaged, preserves induced gamma -- spec 6.3), .freqs (linspace flo..fhi, Nf), .t (s rel onset), .fs, .cfg, .included (trial mask passed through). Provide tfr.bandMask = freqs>=25 & freqs<=58 for the ridge stage.

chirp_ridge INPUT: a single-trial (or the trial-averaged) power TFR slice restricted to the ridge band 25-58 Hz: tfm = tfr.power(bandMask,:,trial) (or meanPower for anchors). Convert to a tfridge-friendly magnitude: tfridge tracks the MAX-energy path, so pass tfm directly (already power); use f = freqs(bandMask).

chirp_ridge PRIMARY RIDGE: [fhat, iRidge, ~] = tfridge(tfm, f, penalty, 'NumRidges',1, 'NumFrequencyBins', nbins). penalty: tfridge penalizes per-step frequency jumps by penalty*(freqDiff^2)/(meanFreq*dt-ish); set penalty so a physiological downchirp (Df up to ~10 Hz over ~0.5-1 s, i.e. <=~20 Hz/s -> <=0.04 Hz/sample at fs=500) is NOT penalized but spurious jumps to a noise peak are. Recommend penalty in the range that suppresses >5 Hz single-sample jumps: start penalty ~= 1 (with f in Hz, df<=1) and CALIBRATE in Phase 0 against the single nonlinear-sweep sims so the recovered ridge tracks the true IF within ~1 Hz. NumFrequencyBins (smoothing/forbidden-zone half-width) ~= 2 bins (~2 Hz) -- enough to bridge a 1-sample dropout without letting the ridge wander across a 5-10 Hz gap. Read ridgePower(t) = tfm(iRidge(t), t) along the path.

chirp_ridge SECOND-RIDGE PEELING: after extracting ridge 1, zero out (peel) its TF support: for each t, set tfm(max(1,iRidge(t)-W) : min(end,iRidge(t)+W), t) = 0, with peeling band-removal half-width W = ceil(peelHz/df) and peelHz ~= 4 Hz (so ~+-4 Hz, full notch ~8 Hz < the 5-10 Hz Df so a genuine second tone survives but the primary ridge's main lobe is removed). Re-run tfridge(NumRidges 1) on the peeled TFR -> candidate ridge 2 (f2hat, ridgePower2).

chirp_ridge SURROGATE SIGNIFICANCE for ridge 2: generate Nsurr (200-1000) per-trial FFT phase-randomized surrogates of the broadband-band signal that produced this trial (NOT of the TFR -- randomize the time-domain signal's FFT phases preserving magnitude), push each through chirp_tfr_faslt (reuse cached kernels) + the SAME peel+re-extract, and record the peeled-ridge integrated energy (sum of ridgePower2 over the transition window). Keep ridge 2 only if observed peeled-ridge energy > 95th percentile of the surrogate distribution. nRidgesSig = 1 + (ridge2 significant). Spec 6.4 + Appendix surrogate spec.

chirp_ridge TRANSITION WINDOW: derive from fhat(t) on the primary ridge. Smooth fhat (e.g. movmedian ~50-100 ms). Define transition = the contiguous span where |d fhat/dt| exceeds a small threshold (frequency is actively changing) OR, equivalently, the span between where smoothed fhat crosses near f_hi and near f_lo. Concretely: tStart = first time fhat drops below f_hi - 1 Hz; tEnd = first time fhat reaches within 1 Hz of f_lo (its late plateau). Clip to the post-onset region (t>0). Store transitionWin = [tStart tEnd] (s). A long stationary low-freq tail is EXCLUDED (spec 6.0). Also compute coexistWin (full span where a 2nd ridge is present/significant) for the beat test handoff.

chirp_ridge POWER-DIP STATISTIC: along the primary ridge, powerDipStat = min(ridgePower within transitionWin) / mean([max(ridgePower in a pre-transition flank), max(ridgePower in a post-transition flank)]). A sequential hi->lo HANDOVER (two tones, not one sweep) produces a power dip at the crossover -> powerDipStat << 1; a single continuous chirp keeps power up -> powerDipStat ~ 1. Flanks = short windows (~150 ms) just before tStart and just after tEnd within the burst.

chirp_ridge_anchors (subject-average): trace tfridge ONCE on tfr.meanPower (band-limited 25-58 Hz). f_hi = ridge frequency at the ~20th-percentile transition time, f_lo = at the ~80th-percentile transition time; clamp BOTH to [27,56] Hz. These are rough (onset jitter smears the average inward -> they read INWARD of the true extremes) and feed ONLY the phase-test crossing times, the spatial band centers, and figure annotations; the chirplet never uses them (spec 6.4).

OUTPUT ASSEMBLY: chirp_ridge returns per-trial struct matching spec 7.1 sub.ridge.trial(i): {fhat[], ridgePower[], nRidgesSig, ridgeOverlap, powerDipStat, transitionWin, burstTruncated, included}. ridgeOverlap = fraction of the trial duration where ridge2 is significant AND within Df of ridge1's band (the coexistence fraction). burstTruncated is passed in from epoching (O15 next-onset truncation, spec 2.3). included = trial QC mask from upstream. Anchors returned separately (per channel/subject), stored in sub.phaseTest.params.{f_hi,f_lo}.

params.name: FASLT flo / fhi
params.rationale: Spec 6.2: pad beyond the 25-58 Hz ridge band for context so the ridge band has no edge artifact at 25 or 58.

params.name: FASLT df (freq step)
params.rationale: Spec: freq step <=1 Hz. 1 Hz resolves a 5-10 Hz Df everywhere and keeps the kernel bank small enough to cache.

params.name: FASLT base cycles c1
params.rationale: Spec 6.2 base cycles ~3; matches nfaslt's c1 semantics (n_cyc = i_ord*c1 with mult=1).

params.name: FASLT order [olo ohi], mult
params.rationale: Spec: adaptive order ~3-30. Multiplicative superresolution gives the smooth high-resolution sweep the spec asks for; low order at low freq, high order toward 70 Hz.

params.name: Ridge band
params.rationale: Spec 6.4: tfridge runs within 25-58 Hz (the OB gamma band, below line noise).

params.name: tfridge penalty
params.rationale: Must permit a real downchirp (<=~20 Hz/s) yet forbid jumps across the 5-10 Hz gap to a noise peak. Calibrated against single nonlinear-sweep sims to track true IF within ~1 Hz (spec 5.4).

params.name: tfridge NumRidges / NumFrequencyBins
params.value: NumRidges=1 (extract sequentially via peeling); NumFrequencyBins~=2 bins (~2 Hz)
params.rationale: Spec 6.4 requires PEELING (not NumRidges=2), because a simultaneous 2nd ridge must be surrogate-gated, not just the 2nd-strongest path. 2-bin smoothing bridges single-sample dropouts without letting the ridge cross the Df gap.

params.name: Peeling band-removal half-width W (peelHz)
params.rationale: Wide enough to remove the primary ridge main lobe, narrow enough that a genuine 2nd tone separated by 5-10 Hz survives the peel.

params.name: Surrogates
params.rationale: Appendix + spec 6.4: time-domain phase randomization preserves the power spectrum, so a 2nd ridge surviving means genuine extra TF structure, not chance.

params.name: Anchor percentiles & clamp
params.value: f_hi at 20th-pctile transition time, f_lo at 80th; clamp [27,56] Hz
params.rationale: Spec 6.4: rough anchors from the subject-average ridge; clamp keeps them inside the analysis band away from the 25/58 edges.

params.name: Transition detection threshold
params.value: fhat crosses f_hi-1 Hz to within 1 Hz of f_lo plateau (movmedian ~75 ms smooth)
params.rationale: Spec 6.0: transition = frequency-changing region only; excludes the stationary low-freq tail that would just add noise/atoms to phase + chirplet tests.

pitfalls: Do NOT derive phase or envelope from the FASLT output -- it is geometric-mean-pooled POWER, not an analytic signal. Phase/envelope MUST come from hilbert() of the 25-58 Hz bandpassed broadband signal (KEY API FACT + anti-bias rule (a)). chirp_tfr_faslt returns power only; the phase test (6.5) takes fhat from THIS ridge as the IF source, never dphi/dt.

Anti-bias (a): fhat from this ridge is the power-based IF that the phase test integrates. If anyone wires dphi/dt of the broadband Hilbert phase in as fhat, resid==0 and the test is vacuous. The ridge IS the independent f-hat; document ifSource='ridgePower' in sub.phaseTest.params.

tfridge tracks the MAXIMUM-energy path and will happily snap to a transient noise peak; if penalty is too low the ridge fragments, too high it ignores a real downchirp. This is the single most important Phase-0 calibration; verify on the nonlinear single-sweep sims before trusting any real ridge.

Kernel caching is load-bearing: nfaslt rebuilds the entire wavelet cell + recomputes padding on every call. With surrogates (200-1000) x trials (40 cue) x sessions, calling vanilla nfaslt per surrogate is the batch bottleneck the spec flags for the lab desktop. Cache the bank keyed on (fs,flo,fhi,Nf,c1,olo,ohi,mult).

Peeling width must be < Df: if W (full notch) >= the 5-10 Hz gap, peeling the primary ridge also erases a genuine second tone and you will never find nRidgesSig=2 -> biases toward 'single'. Keep full notch ~8 Hz at most and confirm against Phase-0 dual sims that true 2nd ridges survive.

Transition window must EXCLUDE the stationary low-frequency tail (a 3 s burst often plateaus). Feeding the tail to the phase/chirplet tests adds noise and atoms (spec 6.0, 6.7). The dip statistic flanks must sit inside the burst, not in baseline (pick them adjacent to tStart/tEnd, within the gamma-present span).

powerDipStat denominator: if a flank max is taken from a near-silent region it explodes the ratio. Anchor flanks to the burst envelope (where ridgePower is still substantial), and guard against div-by-~0 / empty transition windows (set powerDipStat=NaN, mark trial not-included for the dip read).

Surrogate ridge energy must be integrated over the SAME transition window as the observed trial, using the SAME peel+re-extract, or the 95th-pctile threshold is not comparable. Reuse cached kernels for the surrogate TFRs.

Anchors are deliberately rough/inward-biased (onset jitter smears the subject-average ridge). Do not treat f_hi/f_lo as ground truth Df; the chirplet engine must never consume them (spec 6.4), and the beat test should derive |f_hi-f_lo| with that caveat noted.

burstTruncated (O15 next-onset cut, spec 2.3) must propagate into ridge output so a coexistence/transition window cut short by truncation is not mistaken for a genuinely brief one in the beat/chirplet downstream.
designs.mapsToHypothesis: "This component is upstream of the adjudicating tests; it does not itself emit single/dual but supplies the substrate. Its discriminating outputs: (1) nRidgesSig -- a surrogate-significant SECOND ridge coexisting with the first leans DUAL (two simultaneous slowly-varying components, the spec 0.1 reframing); a single tracked ridge that smoothly descends leans SINGLE. (2) powerDipStat << 1 (deep along-ridge power dip in the transition) is the sequential hi->lo HANDOVER signature -> leans DUAL; powerDipStat ~ 1 (power sustained through the descent) -> SINGLE. (3) The fhat(t) ridge is the engine of the PRIMARY single-channel test (phase continuity 6.5, confirms SINGLE) -- a clean single ridge feeds a concentrated phase residual. The transitionWin/coexistWin gate every other test. A NULL second ridge is inconclusive (could be single, or probe/resolution can't separate) -> contributes to 'undecidable' when other tests are mixed, per spec 0.2/8.1. No p-value is emitted here and none should be multiplied with downstream tests -- this is the same data viewed upstream."
outputs: sub.ridge.trial(i).fhat -- [1 x nT] primary ridge frequency Hz vs t (the power-based IF source for the phase test 6.5)
sub.ridge.trial(i).ridgePower -- [1 x nT] power along the primary ridge
sub.ridge.trial(i).nRidgesSig -- 1 or 2 (1 + surrogate-significant second ridge)
sub.ridge.trial(i).ridgeOverlap -- fraction of trial where a significant 2nd ridge coexists within Df of ridge1 (coexistence fraction)
sub.ridge.trial(i).powerDipStat -- min along-ridge power in transition / mean of flanking maxima (sequential-handover signature)
sub.ridge.trial(i).transitionWin -- [tStart tEnd] s rel finalOnset (frequency-changing span; used by chirplet 6.7 + phase 6.5)
sub.ridge.trial(i).burstTruncated -- logical, propagated from O15 next-onset epoch truncation
sub.ridge.trial(i).included -- logical trial QC mask from upstream (never shape-based)
sub.phaseTest.params.f_hi / f_lo -- subject-average ridge anchors, clamped [27,56] Hz (feed phase crossing times, spatial bands, figure annotations only)

tfr.meanPower / tfr.power / tfr.freqs / tfr.t -- the FASLT power TFR (power-averaged across trials) consumed by the single-trial spectrograms (6.3), the temporal-decoupling band envelopes (6.9), and the spatial band powers (6.8)

designs.component: chirp_phase_test.m — segmented phase-continuity test (spec 6.5), the PRIMARY single-channel discriminator. Per OB-channel (bestMac), per-trial: compare the broadband-gamma Hilbert phase increment against the ridge-IF-predicted increment over short consecutive sub-windows of the transition window; concentrated near-zero residual across trials => strong-for-single, dispersed => inconclusive. Asymmetric (spec 0.2): a positive (concentrated) result confirms single; a null never confirms dual.
designs.functionSignature:
function sub = chirp_phase_test(epochs, fhat, ridgeT, transWin, fs, cfg)
% INPUTS
%   epochs   : [nSamp x nTrial] sniff-locked broadband epochs of ONE OB channel
%              (bestMac), already padded beyond [-1,+3]s for edge-free filtering
%              (trim handled internally via cfg.trimSamp). Samples @ fs=500.
%   fhat     : [nT x nTrial] POWER-ridge instantaneous frequency f-hat(t) (Hz)
%              from tfridge on the FASLT power TFR (chirp_ridge_extract.m). MUST be
%              the power ridge, NEVER dphi/dt (rule a). NaN where no ridge.
%   ridgeT   : [1 x nT] time axis (s, 0 = finalOnset) on which fhat is sampled.
%   transWin : [tStart tEnd] (s) per-trial OR [nTrial x 2] transition window from
%              the ridge (§6.4); phase test runs only inside it.
%   fs       : 500.
%   cfg      : struct of params (see PARAMS). Carries beatNullTimes per trial
%              (from chirp_beating) for optional slip-latency tagging; may be [].
% OUTPUT (maps to spec 7.1 sub.phaseTest)
%   sub.params, sub.trial(i), sub.summary  (see OUTPUTS)
steps: VALIDATE INPUTS / GUARD vacuity (rule a): assert fhat was passed as a separate power-ridge array and is NOT derived from the epoch phase. Hard-error if size(fhat,2)~=size(epochs,2) or if cfg.ifSource is not the literal 'ridgePower'. This is the single most important guard: using dphi/dt as f-hat makes resid identically 0 and the test vacuous.

BANDPASS broadband-gamma: filt = ft_preproc_bandpassfilter(epochs', fs, [25 58], [], 'firws')' (zero-phase FIR, transition handled by firws; operate on the PADDED epoch so filter edge transients live in the pad). No in-band notch (58 Hz ceiling clears line noise). Demean+detrend each column first.

ANALYTIC SIGNAL: z = hilbert(filt); phi = unwrap(angle(z)) per trial (column-wise unwrap over the full padded epoch BEFORE trimming, so unwrap has no edge break). env = abs(z) retained only for optional existence gate (step 4). Trim the pad to the analysis span using cfg.trimSamp so phi/ridge share a sample grid.

OPTIONAL existence gate (rule b: response-EXISTENCE only, never shape): if cfg.requireResponse, mark trial included=false when median in-transition broadband-gamma power < cfg.minRespZ * baseline (baseline = pre-sniff [-0.5 -0.1]s). This only avoids computing phase on pure noise; a kept-but-noisy trial is acceptable (it just adds residual dispersion). Do NOT reject on chirp/ridge shape.

RESAMPLE f-hat onto the epoch sample grid: interp1(ridgeT, fhat(:,i), tEpoch, 'linear') so phiPred can be integrated at sample resolution. Drop trial (included=false, reason='noRidge') if fhat is NaN over >cfg.maxRidgeGap of the transition window.
DEFINE per-trial transition window [t0 t1] from transWin(i,:); clamp to where fhat is finite. Skip trial if (t1-t0) < cfg.minTransSec (too short to host even one sub-window).

TILE the transition window into consecutive non-overlapping sub-windows of length cfg.subWinSec (~0.15 s = ~4-8 gamma cycles). Each sub-window short enough that integrated IF-bias accumulation << 1 cycle (long-burst correction: NEVER one t_hi->t_lo increment across the whole multi-second transition).

PER SUB-WINDOW k: phiObsInc(k) = phi(end_k) - phi(start_k) (observed unwrapped Hilbert phase increment, in rad). phiPredInc(k) = 2*pi * trapz(tEpoch(idx_k), fhat_i(idx_k)) (predicted increment from integrating the POWER ridge IF over the sub-window). resid(k) = wrapToPi(phiObsInc(k) - phiPredInc(k)).

PER-TRIAL SUMMARY: store subWinResid (vector over k). Compute mean resultant length meanRbar = abs(mean(exp(1i*resid))) across that trial's sub-windows (circular concentration of the residual). Record nSub used.

SLIP-LATENCY tagging (localizes beating, distinct from dispersion): flag sub-windows whose |resid| exceeds cfg.slipThresh rad as phase slips; store slipLatencies = sub-window center times. If cfg.beatNullTimes(i) provided, additionally record whether slips coincide (within cfg.slipTolSec) with beat nulls — two beating oscillators produce slips LOCALIZED to beat nulls; a single oscillator stays concentrated in EVERY sub-window.

POOL across trials for the session-level residual concentration: collect ALL sub-window residuals from all included trials into one vector R. Rbar = abs(mean(exp(1i*R))). Rayleigh test (rayleigh_z = nR*Rbar^2, rayleigh_p). V-TEST against preferred direction 0 (we predict concentration AT zero residual, not just non-uniformity): vtest_p_vs0 = V-test of R against mu0=0.

PER-SESSION PERMUTATION NULL (absorbs n-dependence per spec 8): for b=1..cfg.nPerm, rotate each trial's residual vector by an independent uniform random phase offset (resid + 2*pi*rand, then wrapToPi) -> null Rbar_b. perm_z = (Rbar_obs - mean(Rbar_null)) / std(Rbar_null); perm_p = (1+sum(Rbar_null>=Rbar_obs))/(1+nPerm). Rotation preserves within-trial residual STRUCTURE but destroys the at-zero alignment, giving the correct H0 (single oscillator => alignment at 0 => high perm_z).

WRITE sub.phaseTest.params / .trial(i) / .summary (spec 7.1). Set nUsed = #included trials. GROUP HOOK: the driver collects perm_z per session; group test (spec 8) is a one-sample t of perm_z>0 across sessions PLUS a group V-test against 0; non-significant => inconclusive (NOT dual). Also save the per-trial figure overlay hook (resid vs sub-window time) under singleTrialSpectrograms/ if cfg.saveFigs.

params.name: ifSource
params.rationale: Hard literal flag asserted at entry. Documents and ENFORCES rule (a): f-hat is the power-based ridge, never dphi/dt of the broadband phase. Any other value errors.

params.name: filtBand
params.rationale: Broadband-gamma FIR passband (spec 6.1 / appendix). 58 Hz ceiling clears line noise so no in-band notch is needed; matches the chirplet/ridge band.

params.name: filtType
params.rationale: ft_preproc_bandpassfilter firws = zero-phase FIR; no phase distortion of the Hilbert phase (any IIR group delay would corrupt phiObsInc).

params.name: subWinSec
params.rationale: ~150 ms consecutive sub-windows = ~4-8 gamma cycles; short enough that integrated IF-bias accumulation is << 1 cycle (a 0.5 Hz IF bias over 0.15 s = 0.075 cycle vs 1.5 cycles over 3 s). The core long-burst correction (spec 6.5).

params.name: minTransSec
params.rationale: Require >=2 sub-windows of transition before a trial can contribute, so per-trial Rbar is not a single-point artifact.

params.name: trimSamp
params.value: round([-1.0 3.0]*fs) relative to onset, with >=0.5 s pad each side already present
params.rationale: Filter+Hilbert run on the padded epoch; trim AFTER unwrap so edge transients and unwrap breaks stay in the discarded pad (spec 2.3 'pad beyond, then trim').

params.name: requireResponse
params.rationale: Optional existence-only gate (rule b). Excludes pure-noise trials from phase computation; never rejects on chirp shape (which would bias toward single).

params.name: minRespZ
params.rationale: Existence threshold: median in-transition gamma power must exceed 1 SD over the pre-sniff baseline. Loose on purpose — only screens truly absent responses.

params.name: maxRidgeGap
params.rationale: Drop a trial if the power ridge is NaN over >25% of its transition window (no reliable f-hat to integrate).

params.name: slipThresh
params.rationale: A sub-window residual past +-90 deg is a phase slip; used to localize discontinuities at beat nulls (the dual signature) rather than to reject.

params.name: slipTolSec
params.rationale: Window for matching a slip latency to a beat null from chirp_beating; ~half a beat period at Df=5-10 Hz.

params.name: nPerm
params.rationale: Per-session permutation null (rotate residuals to uniform). 1000 gives stable perm_z and perm_p resolution ~1e-3; matches surrogate count used elsewhere in the spec.

params.name: beatNullTimes
params.rationale: If supplied, enables slip-vs-beat-null coincidence tagging; absent => slips still recorded by latency, just not cross-referenced.

params.name: saveFigs
params.rationale: Off in batch; driver flips on for the one profiled session to emit resid-vs-time overlays under singleTrialSpectrograms/.

pitfalls: VACUOUS-TEST TRAP (the spec's #1 anti-bias rule): if f-hat is taken as dphi/dt of the same broadband phase, phiPredInc == phiObsInc and resid == 0 for every trial, making the test always 'single'. The ifSource='ridgePower' assert and the separate-array fhat input exist solely to prevent this — do not 'simplify' by deriving f-hat inside the function.

UNWRAP ACROSS EDGES: unwrap must run on the full padded epoch before trimming. Unwrapping a trimmed segment can insert a spurious 2*pi jump at the boundary, corrupting phiObsInc of the first sub-window.

CUMULATIVE IF-BIAS (long-burst): integrating a biased ridge IF over a multi-second window wraps phase (0.5 Hz over 3 s = 1.5 cycles). Never compute a single increment across the whole transition; the sub-window tiling is mandatory, not cosmetic.
RIDGE/PHASE GRID MISMATCH: fhat is sampled on ridgeT (often coarser than fs); interp1 onto the epoch sample grid before trapz, otherwise phiPredInc is integrated on the wrong abscissa.
SHAPE-BASED REJECTION (rule b): do not drop 'messy' or non-chirp-looking trials. Only the existence gate is allowed. Removing dispersed-residual trials would manufacture a single-oscillator result.

P-VALUE MULTIPLICATION (spec 0.2): this test is asymmetric and shares data with the other tests. Report perm_z / vtest_p as ONE element of the per-session verdict vector; do NOT combine it multiplicatively with beating/spatial p-values.

n-DEPENDENCE: raw Rayleigh z scales with n(sub-windows), which differs across sessions (variable burst length). Use the per-session permutation perm_z (rotation null) as the session summary fed to the group test, not raw Rayleigh z.

FIRWS TRANSITION WIDTH: leaving the firws transition band default can pass low-frequency drift into the 'gamma' phase; demean+detrend first and verify the realized passband edges on a Phase-0 synthetic single chirp.
designs.mapsToHypothesis: POSITIVE (strong-for-SINGLE): residuals concentrated near 0 in EVERY sub-window -> high session Rbar, significant V-test against 0, large positive perm_z; at group level a significant one-sample t of perm_z>0 plus group V-test against 0 => 'single' contribution to the verdict vector. NULL (dispersed residuals, perm_z ~ 0, n.s. V-test): INCONCLUSIVE, never 'dual' — dispersion is also produced by a single oscillator with variable timing/noise (spec table, 0.2). DUAL SIGNATURE (supporting, not from dispersion alone): phase slips LOCALIZED to beat nulls (slipLatencies coinciding with chirp_beating null times) lean dual; without that localization a null reads as inconclusive. UNDECIDABLE: mixed across sub-windows/trials, or the regime is Phase-0-flagged undecidable -> contributes 'undecidable' to the per-session verdict (spec 0.2/8.1). This test alone can confirm single but can never, by itself, confirm dual.
outputs: sub.phaseTest.params = { f_hi, f_lo, subWinLen (=subWinSec), filterSpec (=[25 58]+firws), ifSource='ridgePower' } (spec 7.1)

sub.phaseTest.trial(i) = { subWinResid[ (rad, per sub-window) ], meanRbar (per-trial circular resultant length), slipLatencies[ (s, sub-window centers exceeding slipThresh; flagged if coincident with beatNull) ], included (logical; reason recorded when false: noRidge/tooShort/noResponse) } (spec 7.1)

sub.phaseTest.summary = { nUsed (# included trials), Rbar (pooled over all sub-windows), rayleigh_z, rayleigh_p, vtest_p_vs0 (V-test against mu0=0), perm_z (rotation-null z, the n-robust session summary fed to group t-test), perm_p } (spec 7.1)
Per-trial figure hook (when cfg.saveFigs): resid-vs-sub-window-time overlay saved as sub-<sessID>_ch-<chi>_trial-<NNN>_phase.png under <id>/singleTrialSpectrograms/ (spec 2.5)

designs.component: chirp_beat_test.m / chirp_temporal_decoup.m / chirp_spatial.m (cueTask, fs=500). Three new functions under helperFuncs\. Designed against spec sections 6.6 (envelope beating), 6.9 (temporal decoupling), 6.8 (spatial profile), output contract 7.1, anti-bias rules (a)-(e). Engines: nfaslt(input[buf x samp],Fs,[flo fhi],Nf,c1,[olo ohi],mult)->POWER[F x T]; phase/envelope from hilbert() of ft_preproc_bandpassfilter('firws',25-58). Channel selection by contains(label,'macBP'), never row index. Verdicts ASYMMETRIC: beat+ => dual, spatial-dissimilar => dual, decoupled latency => leans dual; nulls inconclusive; mixed => 'undecidable'.

[beat, dec, spat] from three functions:
1) function beat = chirp_beat_test(bb, env, ridge, fs, cfg)  % bb=broadband-gamma epochs[nSamp x nTrial] (25-58 FIR), env=abs(hilbert(bb)) precomputed or []=> compute internally; ridge=per-trial struct array with .transitionWin .fhat (for coexistWin/anchors); cfg has fBeat anchor (|f_hi-f_lo|), envFitOrder, hpCutoff(<=3 or NaN), baselineWin, matchedPowerWin, surrogateSpec, minBeatCycles
2) function dec = chirp_temporal_decoup(tfr, freqs, times, ridge, fHi, fLo, cfg)  % tfr=per-trial FASLT power[F x T x nTrial] (or cell), freqs/times axes, fHi/fLo anchors, cfg.band(+-Hz) .smoothMs
3) function spat = chirp_spatial(epochMacBP, macLabs, goodMac, contactGeom, fs, fHi, fLo, cfg)  % epochMacBP=[nMacBP x nSamp x nTrial] all macBP* channels, goodMac=logical over macBP passing QC, contactGeom=numeric pair-position/spacing, cfg.fHiBand .fLoBand .earlyWin .lateWin
steps: chirp_beat_test (spec 6.6, rule d): for each trial, take env=abs(hilbert(bb)) restricted to the COEXISTENCE window (ridge.transitionWin extended to full two-component span, NOT the stationary tail). Demean.

Remove onset/offset SHAPE only: subtract a fitted low-order polynomial (cfg.envFitOrder, default 2-3) — OR the Model-A reconstruction envelope if available. Do NOT high-pass at 10 Hz. If filtering at all, hpCutoff must be < min Df (<=3 Hz); default cfg.hpCutoff=NaN (no HP). resid = env - fittedTrend.

Spectrum of resid (pwelch or single-window FFT given long window; zero-pad for bin resolution). fBeat anchor = |f_hi - f_lo| from cfg. modSNR = power in fBeat bin / mean(power in flanking bins excluding fBeat +-1 bin). modIndex = peak-to-trough depth of resid normalized by mean env (AM depth at fBeat).

Require nBeatCycles = (coexistWin duration)*fBeat >= cfg.minBeatCycles (default 2); set included=false and record nBeatCycles if too short (a truncated window cannot masquerade as brief — carry burstTruncated from ridge).

deepNullPeriodicity: detect deep periodic nulls directly — find local minima of env, test their spacing concentrates at 1/fBeat (resultant length of null-interval phases). Comparable-amplitude dual => deep regular nulls.

Repeat the SAME resid-spectrum pipeline in the baseline window (pre-sniff) and a matched-power later window; store modSNR_baseline, modSNR_matchedPower as contrasts (beat must exceed both controls to count as dual evidence).

Surrogates (cfg.surrogateSpec, ~200-1000 per-trial FFT phase-randomization of bb): recompute env-resid spectrum; modSNR significant if > 95th pct of surrogate modSNR at fBeat. Populate sub.beating.trial(i) {fBeat,modSNR,modIndex,nBeatCycles,deepNullPeriodicity,modSNR_baseline,modSNR_matchedPower,included}.

chirp_temporal_decoup (spec 6.9): per trial build band-limited power envelopes at f_hi and f_lo by integrating tfr power over freqs in [fHi-band,fHi+band] and [fLo-band,fLo+band] (band default +-2-3 Hz), then smooth (cfg.smoothMs).

Find peak LATENCY of the hi-band envelope (latHi) and lo-band envelope (latLo) within the transition window relative to onset; latDiff=latLo-latHi. Store per trial {latHi,latLo,latDiff,included}. included=false if either band has no suprathreshold peak (existence-only gate, rule b — never shape-based).

Group/session summary: across included trials corrHiLo = Pearson corr(latHi,latLo); varLatDiff = var(latDiff). Rigid coupling (corr->1, low var) leans single; decoupled (corr below Phase-0 single-chirp calibration, high var) leans dual. Store {corrHiLo,varLatDiff,nUsed}.

chirp_spatial (spec 6.8, gated): eligibility first — nGoodContacts=sum(goodMac & on-bulb & adequately spaced from contactGeom). eligible = nGoodContacts>=2 (>=3 preferred). Record spatial.eligible,nGoodContacts,contactSpacing ALWAYS, even when ineligible (so group can distinguish 'not assessed' from 'matched' — spec 8.1).

If eligible: for each good macBP contact and each trial, compute early-high-band power = mean tfr power in fHiBand over earlyWin, and late-low-band power = mean tfr power in fLoBand over lateWin (per-contact FASLT or bandpassed-hilbert power).

Per trial form profileHi (vector over good contacts of early-hi power) and profileLo (vector of late-lo power); normalize each vector. profileSim = correlation (and cosine) of profileHi vs profileLo across contacts. Two generators => low sim; one oscillator predicts identical early/late topography => high sim.

Spatial summary: meanProfileSim across trials, nUsed; carry eligible,nGoodContacts,contactSpacing. Note bipolar caveat in a field/comment: a null (high sim) on coarse/few contacts is WEAK dual-against evidence (macBP is itself a spatial high-pass), so geometry travels with the verdict.

All three return structs shaped to merge into sub.beating / sub.temporalDecoup / sub.spatial (spec 7.1) with .params .trial(i) .summary; each trial row also keyed for the tidy CSVs (session,channel,trial,task,sniffLabel) by the caller.

params.name: cfg.envFitOrder (beat)
params.rationale: Low-order polynomial removes the gamma burst onset/offset SHAPE (a slow <<Df trend) without touching a 5-10 Hz beat. Spec rule d forbids a 10 Hz HP; a 2nd-3rd order poly is the spec's named alternative.

params.name: cfg.hpCutoff (beat)
params.rationale: Spec rule d: NEVER 10 Hz (would destroy the 5-10 Hz beat). Long window gives ~1/T resolution so a plain detrended spectrum isolates Df; any HP cutoff must be below min Df (3 Hz).

params.name: cfg.minBeatCycles (beat)
params.rationale: Spec 6.6/appendix: require >=2 beat cycles in the coexistence window before trusting modSNR; fewer cannot establish periodicity. nBeatCycles = coexistDur*fBeat.

params.name: cfg.surrogateSpec (beat)
params.rationale: Spec appendix; per-trial phase-randomization preserves power spectrum, destroys phase structure -> null distribution for modSNR at fBeat without assuming Gaussian noise.

params.name: fBeat anchor (beat)
params.value: |f_hi - f_lo| from subject-average TFR ridge, clamped [27,56]->Df
params.rationale: Spec 6.4: anchors are read once from the subject-average power-TFR ridge; they feed the beat fBeat bin. Df likely 5-10 Hz (spec 0.3).

params.name: cfg.band (decoup)
params.rationale: Spec 6.8/appendix spatial-band default reused for the band-limited envelopes; wide enough to capture the component, narrow enough to separate a 5-10 Hz gap.

params.name: cfg.smoothMs (decoup)
params.rationale: Smooth the band-limited power envelope so peak-latency is robust to single-cycle ripple without blurring the hi-vs-lo latency gap.

params.name: cfg.earlyWin / cfg.lateWin (spatial)
params.rationale: Spec 6.4 anchor times: f_hi read early, f_lo read late; the spatial bands use the matching early/late windows so hi/lo topographies are read where each dominates.

params.name: spatial eligibility (spatial)
params.rationale: Spec 6.8 gate; recorded as first-class output (eligible,nGoodContacts,contactSpacing) so the group step never conflates 'not assessed' with 'matched' (spec 8.1).

params.name: FASLT range/order (shared TFR input)
params.rationale: Spec 6.2: pad beyond 25-58 for context; nfaslt returns POWER, so envelope/phase for the beat test come from hilbert() of the bandpassed signal, never from FASLT (key API fact).

pitfalls: BEAT: do NOT high-pass the envelope at 10 Hz (spec rule d) — it annihilates a 5-10 Hz beat. Remove only the onset/offset shape with a low-order poly (or Model-A reconstruction); any filter cutoff < min Df (<=3 Hz).

BEAT/all: envelope and phase must come from hilbert() of the bandpassed broadband signal. nfaslt returns POWER (magnitude^2, geometric-mean pooled) — taking 'phase' or a clean analytic envelope from FASLT is wrong (key API fact).

PHASE coupling (sibling test, respect here): never derive f-hat from dphi/dt of the broadband phase; the beat/decoup tests assume f_hi/f_lo come from the power-based ridge (rule a). Anchors clamp to [27,56].
QC: no shape-based trial rejection anywhere (rule b) — would bias toward 'single'. Only an existence gate (any gamma response) sets included=false; a response-free trial may stay and just add noise.

BEAT minimum cycles: a truncated coexistence window (O15 next-onset cut, burstTruncated) must NOT be scored as a genuinely brief overlap — carry burstTruncated and require nBeatCycles>=2 honestly (spec 2.3).

SPATIAL: always record eligible/nGoodContacts/contactSpacing even when ineligible, so group logic separates 'not assessed' from 'profiles matched' (spec 8.1). Never average absent-spatial with negative-spatial.

SPATIAL bipolar caveat: macBP referencing is itself a spatial high-pass; a high-similarity (null) result on few/coarse contacts is WEAK against dual — geometry must travel with the verdict (spec 6.8).

ASYMMETRY: beat-absent / sim-high / latency-coupled are INCONCLUSIVE, not proof of single. Do not multiply these p-values as independent (spec 0.2) — return per-test directional evidence for the verdict vector.
Channels by label (contains(...,'macBP')), never fixed row index — montages vary by session (CLAUDE.md, spec 2.2). Scalp/EEG rows 1-32 are EXCLUDED from spatial (spec 6.8).
Epoch on behDat.finalOnset not sniffOnset; pad beyond [-1,+3] s for edge-free filtering/Hilbert then trim (spec 2.3); behDat is a TABLE — index by name.
designs.mapsToHypothesis: BEAT (chirp_beat_test): a clean beat at fBeat=|f_hi-f_lo| with modSNR > surrogate-95th AND > baseline/matched-power contrasts AND >=2 cycles AND deep periodic nulls => STRONG for DUAL (two coexisting components). Absent beat => INCONCLUSIVE (a single oscillator also has slow AM); never read as 'single'. SPATIAL (chirp_spatial): on an ELIGIBLE session, low hi-vs-lo profileSim (below the within-component split-half ceiling) => STRONG for DUAL (distinct hi/lo topographies). High sim => INCONCLUSIVE (one generator, OR probe/bipolar can't resolve — weak given the bipolar high-pass caveat). Ineligible => 'spatial: not assessed' (distinct state, never folded in). DECOUPLE (chirp_temporal_decoup): corr(latHi,latLo) below the Phase-0 single-chirp calibration and var(latDiff) above it => LEANS DUAL; rigid coupling (corr~1, low var) => leans single. Per-session these three feed the verdict vector with phase/chirplet: defensible single = matched spatial + rigid coupling + no beat (+ concentrated phase + single trajectory); defensible dual = beat present + distinct spatial + decoupled latency (+ two parallel trajectories); mixed or undecidable-regime => report 'undecidable' (spec 0.2, 8.1).
outputs: sub.beating.params {coexistWin, envFitOrder, hpCutoff(<=3 or none), surrogateSpec}
sub.beating.trial(i) {fBeat, modSNR, modIndex, nBeatCycles, deepNullPeriodicity, modSNR_baseline, modSNR_matchedPower, included}
sub.beating.summary {nUsed, medianLogSNR, fracSig, sepBeatSlope}
sub.temporalDecoup.trial(i) {latHi, latLo, latDiff, included}
sub.temporalDecoup.summary {corrHiLo, varLatDiff, nUsed}
sub.spatial.params {fHiBand, fLoBand, earlyWin, lateWin}
sub.spatial.trial(i) {profileHi[over macBP], profileLo[over macBP], profileSim, included}
sub.spatial.summary {eligible(bool), nGoodContacts, contactSpacing, meanProfileSim, nUsed}

function out = chirp_chirplet(seg, fs, transWin, cfg)
% seg      : real 1xN broadband-gamma epoch (25-58 Hz FIR-bandpassed, demeaned/detrended), fs=500
% transWin : [t0 t1] in seconds rel. epoch start = the TRANSITION window from ridge (spec 6.4/6.0); chirplet runs ONLY here
% cfg      : struct of params (see params[]); honors cfg.surrSpec, cfg.Q, cfg.c_tol, cfg.Neff_mode etc.
% out      : per-trial struct -> sub.chirplet.trial(i) fields (spec 7.1)
% NOTE: call mp_adapt_chirplets DIRECTLY (NOT mp_act_signal: it pops a figure; NOT mle_adapt_chirplets: latent EM bug).
steps: PATH SETUP (once, by driver not here): addpath(genpath('C:\Users\Adam\Documents\GitHub\mpact')); register in setup_chirpAnalysis_paths.m / labPaths block so home (Documents\GitHub) and lab (G:\My Drive\GitHub) resolve identically. chirp_chirplet.m lives in helperFuncs\.

INPUT WINDOWING: crop seg to transWin samples idx = round(transWin*fs)+1 (clamp to [1 N]); demean+detrend the crop. Record Ntrans=numel(crop). Guard: if Ntrans < cfg.minTransSamp (default 0.15*fs=75) return out.included=false (transition too short to fit; do NOT fabricate atoms).

ANALYTIC SIGNAL DECISION: build x = hilbert(crop) and feed the ANALYTIC signal to mp_adapt_chirplets (do NOT pass the raw real signal). Rationale: mp_chirplet atoms are complex one-sided (fc in [0,2pi] rad/sample, vub(2)=2*pi); a real signal has +/- frequency images that the MP would fit with mirror-image atoms (negative fc near 2*pi) and spurious cr, corrupting the geometry read. crop is already 25-58 Hz bandpassed so hilbert is clean. (mp_act_signal analytifies internally for exactly this reason; we replicate it but skip its figure + keep the analytic x to bypass the buggy MLE path.)

FIT: P = mp_adapt_chirplets(x, Q, M, D, i0, radix, 'no', mnits, level, 'RefineAlgorithm','expectmax', 'PType','Oneill'). Q=cfg.Q (default 3 -> allow a curved single sweep to use 2-3 LINKED atoms per rule c; never 0 -> ginput). verbose='no' MANDATORY. P is Q-by-5 O'Neill rows [A tc fc cr d].

CONVERT EACH ATOM TO PHYSICAL UNITS: tc_s = (P(:,2)-1)/fs + transWin(1) (tc is sample index within crop, 1-based -> seconds rel. epoch). fc_Hz = P(:,3)*fs/(2*pi). chirp_Hz_per_s = P(:,4)*fs^2/(2*pi). sigma_s = P(:,5)/fs (Gaussian std). amp = abs(P(:,1)); phase = angle(P(:,1)). energyFrac per atom = |A_k|^2 / sum(|A_k|^2) (atoms ~orthonormal in make_chirplets).

ATOM SIGNIFICANCE via phase-randomized surrogates (spec 6.7, rule c uses these for atom keep): generate cfg.nSurr (default 200) FFT-phase-randomized surrogates of crop (preserve magnitude spectrum, randomize phase, enforce conjugate symmetry, ifft -> real, re-hilbert); fit Q=1 chirplet to each; collect surrogate single-atom |A|^2 energyFrac of total signal energy. Keep real atoms whose energyFrac exceeds the 95th percentile of the surrogate distribution. nAtomsSig = count kept. Atoms below threshold are dropped before geometry classification.
FILTER TO GAMMA-BAND ATOMS: discard kept atoms whose fc_Hz outside [22 62] (out-of-band MP artifacts) before trajectory metric. Sort surviving atoms by tc_s ascending.

TRAJECTORY-CONNECTIVITY METRIC (rule c: GEOMETRY not count). With nAtomsSig>=2 sorted by tc: for each consecutive pair (j,j+1) compute (a) temporal adjacency/overlap = whether their +/-1*sigma supports touch: gap_s = tc_s(j+1)-tc_s(j); overlapSpan = min(tc+sigma)-max(tc-sigma); (b) freq step df = fc_Hz(j+1)-fc_Hz(j); (c) chirp-sign agreement = sign(chirp_Hz_per_s(j))==sign(chirp_Hz_per_s(j+1)) and both<=0 (downchirp). CHAIN edge exists (single-like link) iff atoms are temporally adjacent (gap_s <= cfg.chainGap, default 1.5*median(sigma_s)) AND freq descends (df < -cfg.dfMin, default -1 Hz) AND chirp rates same sign. PARALLEL edge (dual-like) iff atoms temporally OVERLAP (overlapSpan>0 i.e. coexist) AND |fc difference| > cfg.dualDf (default 3 Hz, the regime min Df) AND both |chirp_Hz_per_s| <= c_tol. trajConnectivity = (#chain edges)/(#chain + #parallel edges) in [0,1] (1=fully chained, 0=fully parallel); store also nChainEdges, nParallelEdges.

CLASSIFY (single|dual|ambig): SINGLE if nAtomsSig==1 with chirp_Hz_per_s<=-cfg.crMin (one descending atom) OR (nAtomsSig>=2 AND trajConnectivity>=cfg.trajThiSingle (default 0.66) AND no parallel coexisting pair). DUAL if exists >=1 parallel edge: two near-constant-freq (|chirp|<=c_tol) atoms with distinct fc (>dualDf) that temporally COEXIST (overlapSpan>0). AMBIG otherwise (mixed, or atoms neither clearly chained nor clearly parallel, or only 1 atom with |chirp|<crMin i.e. a flat single tone -> cannot distinguish from one of a pair => ambig, report undecidable per rule e).

STRUCTURAL BIC corroboration (Model-A vs Model-B; spec 6.7, only as corroboration). Model A = REFIT with Q=1, c free -> reconstruct xA=make_chirplets(Ntrans,Pa); errA = norm(x-xA)^2. Model B = REFIT with Q=2 then PROJECT each atom's cr toward 0 if |chirp_Hz_per_s|<=c_tol (enforce near-constant-freq) and require distinct fc; reconstruct xB; errB = norm(x-xB)^2. Neff = number of gamma cycles in window = (mean fc_Hz)*Ntrans/fs (NOT raw samples, rule c). BIC_A = Neff*log(errA/Neff) + kA*log(Neff); BIC_B likewise with kB; kA=5 (1 atom x 5 params), kB=10. dBIC = BIC_A - BIC_B (>0 favors B/dual). Store c1=chirp_Hz_per_s of the Model-A atom (the chirp-reality check; expect <0 for a real downchirp).

DERIVE f1,f2,tSep,overlap for output: if dual -> f1,f2 = the two parallel atoms' fc_Hz (hi,lo), tSep = tc_s difference, overlap = overlapSpan (s). If single -> f1=fc of first(early/high) atom, f2=fc of last(late/low) atom along the chain, tSep=span, overlap=NaN. Always store full atoms matrix [tc_s fc_Hz chirp_Hz_per_s sigma_s amp phase energyFrac].

RETURN out struct with all spec-7.1 fields; set out.included=true. The driver loops trials (parfor on lab desktop), preallocates sub.chirplet.trial(i)=out, and computes sub.chirplet.summary across trials (medianC1, fracDownchirp, fracSingleTraj, fracDualTraj).

params.name: Q
params.rationale: Allow up to 3 atoms so a curved (nonlinear) SINGLE sweep can be traced by 2-3 LINKED linear atoms without forcing the classifier to call it dual; geometry (chaining) not count is the discriminator (rule c, spec 6.7). Q>0 mandatory or mp_adapt_chirplets calls ginput and hangs.

params.name: M
params.rationale: Newton-Raphson refinement resolution; MPACT default, adequate at fs=500 over a sub-second transition window. No reason to deviate.

params.name: D
params.rationale: Depth of the Bultan MP dictionary scale decomposition; MPACT default. Controls coarse-grid scale coverage; sigma at burst scales (tens-hundreds ms) is well inside radix^D scales at fs=500.

params.name: i0
params.rationale: First level to rotate chirplets; MPACT default. Rotation from level 1 lets even short atoms acquire chirp, needed to detect the descending sweep.

params.name: radix
params.rationale: Scale radix; MPACT default dyadic dictionary. Fine enough given Newton-Raphson refines off the coarse grid.

params.name: verbose
params.rationale: MANDATORY: 'yes'/'vv' print per-atom tables; combined with Q=0 ginput these block an unattended parfor batch. 'no' keeps the lab-desktop run silent.

params.name: mnits
params.rationale: Max EM refinement iterations; MPACT default. EM (expectmax) refines all atoms jointly each pass; 5 converges on clean band-limited segments. Raise to ~8 in Phase-0 if atom params drift.

params.name: level
params.rationale: MLE difficulty level (passed through but unused on the expectmax branch we take); leave at default 2.

params.name: RefineAlgorithm
params.rationale: Use EM (em_chirplets) joint refinement — robust and the documented MPEM path. AVOID 'maxlikeliest'/mle_chirplets and the wrapper mle_adapt_chirplets (latent EM bug per shared context).

params.name: PType
params.rationale: Return atoms in O'Neill [A tc fc cr d] format so the documented conversions fc_Hz=fc*fs/2/pi, chirp_Hz_per_s=cr*fs^2/2/pi apply directly. Cohen format would change the unit map.

params.name: analyticInput
params.rationale: MP atoms are one-sided complex (fc in [0,2pi], vub=2*pi); a real input spawns mirror-frequency atoms that corrupt the trajectory geometry. crop is 25-58 Hz bandpassed so hilbert is clean. Mirrors mp_act_signal's internal analytify, but we keep control to skip its figure and the MLE path.

params.name: c_tol
params.rationale: spec Appendix default (small |c|, 10-20 Hz/s). An atom flatter than this counts as near-constant-freq for the Model-B / parallel-pair (dual) test; over a 1-3 s window 10 Hz/s drifts <30 Hz, below the regime, so it reads as a tone not a sweep.

params.name: crMin
params.rationale: An atom must descend faster than ~5 Hz/s (lower bound of the likely 5-10 Hz Df over a ~1 s transition) to count as a genuine sweep when classifying a lone atom; below it a single atom is a flat tone => ambig (cannot rule out being one of a dual pair).

params.name: dualDf
params.rationale: Two coexisting near-flat atoms must differ in fc by > 3 Hz (the regime minimum Df, spec 0.3) to be a credible hi/lo dual pair rather than one component split by fit noise.

params.name: dfMin
params.rationale: Consecutive chained atoms must step DOWN in fc by > 1 Hz to count as a descending-chain edge (single-like); smaller steps are within fit jitter.

params.name: chainGap
params.rationale: Two atoms are temporally adjacent (chain) if their centers are within ~1.5 atom-widths; scales with the fitted Gaussian widths rather than a fixed ms so it adapts to burst length.

params.name: trajThiSingle
params.rationale: trajConnectivity (chain/(chain+parallel) edges) >= 0.66 with no coexisting parallel pair => single. Two-thirds-chained tolerates one stray atom in a 3-atom curved sweep.

params.name: nSurr
params.rationale: spec Appendix (200-1000 phase-randomized surrogates, 95th pctile). 200 gives a stable 95th-percentile energy threshold; bump toward 1000 in Phase-0 if the threshold is noisy. Each surrogate is a cheap Q=1 fit.

params.name: minTransSamp
params.rationale: Below ~150 ms the transition cannot resolve a 5 Hz Df (Rayleigh, spec 0.3) so a chirplet fit is meaningless; return included=false rather than fabricate geometry (rule b: no shape-based selection, but a hard existence/length guard is permitted).

pitfalls: Q=0 => mp_adapt_chirplets calls ginput(1) and BLOCKS forever in a headless parfor batch. ALWAYS pass Q>0 (we use 3).
Calling mp_act_signal instead of mp_adapt_chirplets pops a figure per trial (show_decomp) — fatal across thousands of trials on the lab desktop. Call mp_adapt_chirplets directly.
mle_adapt_chirplets / RefineAlgorithm 'maxlikeliest' has a latent EM-branch bug (shared context) — use 'expectmax'.

UNIT TRAP: tc is a 1-based SAMPLE index within the cropped transition window assuming fs=1, NOT seconds and NOT relative to the epoch. Convert tc_s=(tc-1)/fs+transWin(1). fc is rad/sample (0..2pi) NOT Hz; cr is rad/sample^2. Forgetting the fs^2 in chirp_Hz_per_s=cr*fs^2/2/pi makes chirp rates off by 250000x.
fc near 2*pi (i.e. ~fs Hz) is a NEGATIVE-frequency mirror atom from feeding a real (not analytic) signal — guard by analytic input + the [22 62] Hz gamma-band atom filter.

Atom COUNT is NOT the discriminator (rule c): a single nonlinear sweep legitimately needs 2-3 atoms. Classifying on nAtomsSig>=2 => dual would re-introduce the exact single-vs-dual bias the spec forbids. Classify on chain-vs-parallel GEOMETRY (coexistence + flatness), not count.
BIC must use Neff = number of gamma CYCLES in the window, not raw sample count — oscillatory residuals are autocorrelated and raw-N BIC is wildly overconfident toward more atoms (rule c, spec 6.7).
Do NOT impose any shape-based trial rejection here (rule b); the only permitted gate is the minTransSamp length/existence guard. Selecting clean-looking chirps biases toward single.

make_chirplets normalizes each atom (unit norm) and applies a periodization 'PeriodEff' by default; reconstruct with the SAME default ('PeriodEff',true) used internally so errA/errB are consistent with how MP fit them.

The transition window (NOT the full coexistence/burst window) is the fit domain (spec 6.0): forcing atoms across a long stationary low-freq tail adds spurious flat atoms that the parallel-edge test would misread as a dual second component.

A lone flat atom (|chirp|<crMin, nAtomsSig==1) must be classified AMBIG, not single — a single constant-frequency tone is indistinguishable from one member of a dual pair on this test (report undecidable, rule e), not evidence for one oscillator.
designs.mapsToHypothesis: "GEOMETRY, not count (rule c). SINGLE (positive for one-oscillator): significant atoms chain end-to-end into one continuous DESCENDING trajectory (temporally adjacent, fc steps down, chirp rates same negative sign) -> trajConnectivity>=0.66, fracSingleTraj high at group level, and the Model-A chirp c1<0 (real downchirp). DUAL (positive for two-oscillator): >=1 pair of near-constant-frequency atoms (|chirp|<=c_tol) at distinct fc (>dualDf) that TEMPORALLY COEXIST (overlapSpan>0) -> a parallel edge, fracDualTraj high, dBIC>0 favoring Model-B where Phase-0 licenses the structural test. UNDECIDABLE/INCONCLUSIVE (null per rule e): a lone flat atom, mixed chain+parallel edges, or transition too short (included=false) => classification 'ambig'; reported as undecidable, NEVER folded into single or dual. This test is asymmetric (spec 0.2): a clean connected descending chain confirms single; clean coexisting parallel tones confirm dual; everything else is mute. Group adjudication reads fracSingleTraj vs fracDualTraj per session into the verdict vector, not a single p-value."
outputs: atoms : Nsig-by-7 matrix [tc_s, fc_Hz, chirp_Hz_per_s, sigma_s, amp, phase, energyFrac] (sub.chirplet.trial(i).atoms)
nAtomsSig : number of atoms surviving the surrogate-95pct significance + gamma-band filter
trajConnectivity : chainEdges/(chainEdges+parallelEdges) in [0,1] (1=single-like chain, 0=dual-like parallel)
classification : 'single' | 'dual' | 'ambig'
c1 : chirp rate (Hz/s) of the Model-A single free-c atom (the chirp-reality check; <0 = genuine downchirp)
errA : Model-A residual energy norm^2 (1 atom, free c)
errB : Model-B residual energy norm^2 (2 near-constant-freq atoms, |c|<=c_tol, distinct fc)
dBIC : BIC_A - BIC_B with Neff=#gamma cycles (>0 favors dual/Model-B)
f1 : early/high atom center freq (Hz)
f2 : late/low atom center freq (Hz)
tSep : temporal separation of the two relevant atoms (s)
overlap : coexistence span of the parallel pair (s); NaN for a single chain
included : logical; false when transition window < minTransSamp (guard, not shape rejection)

designs.component: Phase-0 validation harness (spec 5) — chirp_synth_trial.m (synthesizer) + chirp_phase0_harness.m (sweep driver + per-test sensitivity/specificity/curve emitter), plus the REAL-DATA burst-length measurement (measure_burst_lengths.m). Gates all interpretation of the Phase-1 battery. New files under helperFuncs\; outputs to a new chirpAnalysis\phase0\ dir. Synth signals are pushed through the SAME Phase-1 test functions (phase continuity §6.5, envelope beating §6.6, chirplet geometry §6.7, ridge §6.4, temporal decoupling §6.9) so the harness measures the actual estimators, not re-implementations.
designs.functionSignature: [trial, gt] = chirp_synth_trial(family, cfg)  % family in {'singleLin','singleNL','dualIndep','dualLocked'}; cfg has fs, overlapMs, Df, ampRatio, fLo, snrDb, burstMs, padMs, fastDropMs, rngSeed. Returns trial.x [1 x Nsamp] (broadband-gamma signal embedded in pink+white noise at empirical SNR, t=0 at sniff onset) and gt (ground-truth struct: family, isDual logical, fHi, fLo, ifTrue(t), coexistWin [t0 t1] s, transitionWin, envTrue, ampHi, ampLo, phaseHi, phaseLo, nGammaCyclesOverlap).  // SWEEP DRIVER: results = chirp_phase0_harness(sweepCfg)  // sweepCfg has overlapGrid=[50 100 200 500 1000 2000] ms, DfGrid=[3 5 7 10] Hz, ampRatioGrid={[1 1],[2 1],[4 1]}, nTrialsPerCell, families, snrDb (from real data), burstLenSampler (from measure_burst_lengths), testBatteryFcns (handles to the Phase-1 functions), outDir, rngSeed, useLabDesktop. Returns/writes results struct + CSV/PNG deliverables.  // REAL DATA: bl = measure_burst_lengths(chanDat_or_outDat, cfg) -> per-trial burst start/stop/length + cross-trial summary used to set burstLenSampler & snrDb.
steps: chirp_synth_trial — TIME BASE: build t from -padMs..(burstMs+padMs) at fs=500 (pad >= longest FASLT/FIR support so later trim is edge-free; default padMs=600). Sniff onset = t=0. All trial families embed the gamma signal starting at t=0 inside a noise floor that exists across the whole epoch (so pre-onset baseline window for beat control exists).

chirp_synth_trial family 'singleLin': ONE oscillator, IF(t) linear from fHi=fLo+Df down to fLo over the burst (downchirp, c<0). Signal = ampHi*cos(2*pi*cumtrapz(t,IF)+phi0). This is the canonical true-single. Envelope = logistic onset (rise ~80 ms) * logistic offset at burst end.

chirp_synth_trial family 'singleNL': ONE oscillator, mildly nonlinear downchirp = fast exponential drop over cfg.fastDropMs (e.g. 300-500 ms) from fHi to near fLo, then a low-frequency plateau at fLo for the remainder (matches spec 5(i): 'fast drop -> low-frequency plateau'). Single connected IF trajectory, monotone non-increasing. This is the family that must be recovered as ONE connected chirplet trajectory even if it needs 2-3 linked atoms (validates geometry-not-count, spec 6.7 / deliverable 3b).

chirp_synth_trial family 'dualIndep': TWO fixed/slowly-varying tones, fHi=fLo+Df and fLo, with INDEPENDENT random phases (phaseHi, phaseLo drawn iid each trial). Each tone gated by its own logistic on/off envelope; the ON-overlap of the two envelopes spans exactly cfg.overlapMs centered in the burst (hi tone earlier-weighted, lo tone later-weighted, but they COEXIST for overlapMs). Sum = ampHi*cos(2*pi*fHi*t+phaseHi).*envHi + ampLo*cos(2*pi*fLo*t+phaseLo).*envLo. Record coexistWin = the overlap span; nGammaCyclesOverlap = overlapMs/1000 * mean([fHi fLo]). This is the canonical true-dual the beat/spatial/phase tests must catch once overlap >> 1/Df.

chirp_synth_trial family 'dualLocked': degenerate dual — same as dualIndep but phaseHi/phaseLo are deterministically phase-locked (fixed offset, NOT redrawn per trial). This is the hard case that mimics a chirp; used to map where every test (including phase continuity) goes inconclusive. Small set per spec.

chirp_synth_trial NOISE & SNR: add colored noise to hit cfg.snrDb where SNR = 10*log10(var(gammaSignal_in_band)/var(noise_in_25-58band)). Use pink (1/f) + white mix so the in-band noise statistics resemble real broadband gamma background; measure noise power inside 25-58 Hz after FIR so the SNR is defined in-band. Default snrDb taken from measure_burst_lengths on real trials (peak gamma power vs pre-onset baseline power, in dB).

chirp_synth_trial AMP RATIO: ampHi/ampLo = cfg.ampRatio (1:1 -> deepest beat nulls / hardest spatial; 4:1 -> dominant component, beat shallow). For single families ampRatio is ignored (one component) — record NaN so sweep cells for single families are not double-counted.

chirp_synth_trial GROUND TRUTH: return gt with everything a test needs to be scored without re-deriving: isDual, fHi, fLo, the true IF(t) (for ridge RMSE), coexistWin & transitionWin (so harness can feed the SAME windows the Phase-1 ridge would derive AND a 'cheat' window to separate window-finding error from test error), per-component envelopes, and nGammaCyclesOverlap (feeds Neff for chirplet BIC scoring).

chirp_phase0_harness SWEEP: triple-nested loop over overlapGrid x DfGrid x ampRatioGrid; inner loop nTrialsPerCell synthetic trials per family. For single families, overlap axis is interpreted as 'transition duration' and ampRatio is fixed/NaN (single families still swept over Df=full sweep extent and burst length so single-specificity is measured across the same regime). Seed RNG per (cell,trial,family) deterministically from rngSeed for reproducibility.

chirp_phase0_harness RUN BATTERY: push EVERY synthetic trial through the ACTUAL Phase-1 functions via testBatteryFcns handles — ridge extraction (FASLT nfaslt 20-70 Hz then DP ridge), phase continuity (segmented ~150 ms sub-windows, f-hat = power-based ridge IF, NEVER dphi/dt — assert this), envelope beating (no >3 Hz HP, env spectrum over coexistWin, modSNR at |fHi-fLo|), chirplet geometry (MPACT mp_adapt_chirplets verbose='no' Q>0, classify single/dual by trajectory connectivity not atom count), temporal decoupling (per-trial latHi/latLo). Cache the FASLT kernel set across trials within a cell (same fs/freq grid).

chirp_phase0_harness SCORING (deliverable 1): for each test x each (overlap,Df,ampRatio) cell compute SENSITIVITY = P(test fires its positive call | family is the one it confirms) and SPECIFICITY = P(test stays null | family is the OTHER hypothesis), respecting test asymmetry (spec 0.2): beat & spatial-proxy & decoupling are scored as dual-detectors (positive on dualIndep, must be null on singleLin/singleNL); phase continuity is scored as a single-detector (concentrated residual on single, dispersed on dual). Store as tables indexed by (test, overlap, Df, ampRatio, family).

chirp_phase0_harness BEAT-MINIMUM-OVERLAP CURVE (deliverable 2): for dualIndep, per Df, find the smallest overlapMs at which >=2 beat cycles are detected AND modSNR exceeds the surrogate 95th pctile in >=X% of trials. Expect recovery once overlapMs >> 1000/Df. Emit beat_min_overlap_vs_Df curve (and its dependence on ampRatio).

chirp_phase0_harness CHIRPLET SINGLE-BIAS CURVE (deliverable 3): on dualIndep trials, plot fraction classified 'single' (Model-A reflexively winning) vs overlap, per Df — must DROP toward 0 once overlap >> 1/Df (bias gone). Separately, on singleNL trials, confirm fraction classified as ONE connected trajectory stays HIGH even though 2-3 atoms are used (report nAtomsSig distribution alongside trajConnectivity to prove the discriminator is geometry, not count).

chirp_phase0_harness PHASE-SEGMENTATION CHECK (deliverable 4): on singleLin/singleNL, compare meanRbar of segmented (~150 ms) vs a single t_hi->t_lo increment across the whole transition; confirm segmented stays concentrated (Rbar high) while unsegmented collapses for transitions > ~1 s (cumulative IF-bias wraps). On dualIndep, confirm phase slips localize to beat nulls (cross-correlate per-sub-window residual magnitude with envelope-null times).

chirp_phase0_harness MINIMUM-COEXISTENCE TABLE (deliverable 5): collapse the sensitivity surfaces into, per test, the minimum overlapMs (per Df, per ampRatio) at which sensitivity>=0.8 & specificity>=0.8. This is the number that bounds the project. Overlay the REAL burst/overlap-length distribution from measure_burst_lengths so each test's teeth-vs-regime is visible at a glance.

chirp_phase0_harness OUTPUTS: write phase0_sensitivity.csv (one row per test x cell x family), beat_min_overlap.csv, chirplet_bias.csv, phase_segmentation.csv, min_coexistence.csv to outDir=chirpAnalysis\phase0\; save PNGs: per-test sensitivity/specificity heatmaps (overlap x Df), beat-minimum-overlap curve, chirplet single-bias curve + singleNL connectivity panel, phase segmented-vs-unsegmented panel, and the min-coexistence-vs-real-burst overlay. Save the full results struct as phase0_results.mat (-v7.3).

measure_burst_lengths (REAL DATA): epoch the OB bestMac channel around behDat.finalOnset ([-1 +3] s, O15 truncate at next finalOnset and set burstTruncated). Compute smoothed gamma-power TS = movmean(ridgePower or abs(hilbert(25-58 FIR))^2, ~50 ms). Per trial find PEAK in (0,3000] ms. Build cross-trial peak distribution; threshold = 75th percentile of that distribution. Burst START = first up-crossing of threshold, STOP = subsequent down-crossing, searching ONLY (0,3000] ms post-onset. length = stop-start. Return per-trial [start stop length peakLat peakVal burstTruncated] and summary {median, IQR, p90 burst length; median peak gamma SNR in dB -> feeds harness snrDb; for dual-plausible coexistence, also the within-burst time the smoothed power spends in its upper tertile as a proxy ceiling on achievable overlap}.

measure_burst_lengths CONFIRM-AGAINST-HARNESS: run on a few O15 and cueTask sessions (bestMac), feed median/IQR burst length into chirp_phase0_harness burstLenSampler and median SNR into snrDb, so the synthetic regime matches reality (spec 5 deliverable 5). This closes the loop: the harness specificity/sensitivity tables are then valid for THIS data's regime.

params.name: fs
params.rationale: Fixed by pipeline (spec App.); 2 ms/sample; gamma 25-58 Hz well within Nyquist.

params.name: overlapGrid (ms)
params.rationale: Primary sweep axis = coexistence duration (spec 0.3/5). 50 ms is sub-beat-cycle (hardest); 2000 ms = 10-40 beat cycles (beat must recover). 1/Df ranges 100-333 ms, so the grid straddles the 1/Df boundary where bias vanishes.

params.name: DfGrid (Hz)
params.rationale: Empirical hi/lo gap is ~5-10 Hz (spec 0.3); 3 Hz is the sub-regime stressor (Rayleigh-marginal at short windows), 10 Hz the easy end.

params.name: ampRatioGrid
params.rationale: 1:1 = deepest beat nulls but hardest spatial/sequential; 4:1 = one component dominates, beat shallow, single-bias strongest. Maps the whole identifiability surface (spec 5).

params.name: fLo (Hz)
params.rationale: Places fHi=fLo+Df inside 25-58 broadband window for all Df, clamped well inside the [27,56] anchor clamp.

params.name: snrDb
params.rationale: Spec 5 requires matching empirical SNR; set in-band (25-58 Hz) from real peak-gamma-vs-baseline so specificity numbers transfer to real data. Never guessed-only.

params.name: burstMs / burstLenSampler
params.rationale: Spec 5: match REAL burst lengths; long bursts make non-overlap segments resolvable, so the worst case is brief overlap (the overlapGrid low end), not short bursts.

params.name: padMs
params.rationale: >= longest FASLT wavelet half-support + FIR group delay at 25 Hz so post-filter/TFR trim to [-1,+3] s is edge-free (mirrors Phase-1 'pad beyond then trim').

params.name: fastDropMs (singleNL)
params.rationale: A 3 s sweep is unlikely perfectly linear (spec 5(i)); fast exp drop then plateau is the realistic single shape that forces 2-3 linked atoms — the geometry-not-count stressor.

params.name: nTrialsPerCell
params.rationale: Enough to estimate sensitivity/specificity to ~+-0.06 at p~0.8 and to drive the cross-trial decoupling correlation; mirrors real per-session trial count.

params.name: phase subWinLen
params.rationale: Spec 6.5/App: ~4-8 gamma cycles, short enough that integrated IF-bias << 1 cycle; harness validates this exact value vs the unsegmented control.

params.name: FASLT range / order
params.rationale: Spec 6.2 / App; pad context beyond 25-58; identical kernel set cached across trials in a cell so the harness exercises the real TFR estimator.

params.name: beat HP cutoff
params.rationale: Spec 6.6 anti-bias rule (d): a 10 Hz HP would destroy a 5-10 Hz beat; cutoff must be < min Df. Harness asserts the test obeys this.

params.name: chirplet Q / verbose / Neff
params.rationale: Q=0 calls ginput (KEY API FACT); verbose='no' mandatory; structural BIC uses Neff=cycles not samples (spec 6.7 anti-bias rule c). Use mp_adapt_chirplets / mp_act_signal (mle_adapt_chirplets EM branch has a latent bug).

params.name: surrogates
params.rationale: Spec App / 6.4/6.7; per-trial null for ridge-2 energy, atom significance, beat modSNR threshold.

params.name: rngSeed
params.rationale: Deterministic per-(cell,trial,family) seeding so sweep is reproducible and re-runnable on lab desktop without drift.

pitfalls: dphi/dt CONTAMINATION (spec anti-bias a): if the phase test's f-hat is taken from the broadband Hilbert phase derivative instead of the power-based ridge, the residual is identically 0 and BOTH the test and the harness scoring become vacuous (single-detector reports 100% sensitivity for free). The harness MUST call the same phase-test function the real pipeline uses and assert ifSource=='ridgePower'.

SHAPE-BASED SELECTION leaking in (spec anti-bias b): synth trials must NOT be filtered for 'clean' beats/chirps before scoring — that would inflate specificity. Only the optional existence check is allowed; a response-free synthetic trial just adds noise.

BEAT HP at 10 Hz (anti-bias d): a 10 Hz envelope high-pass annihilates a 5-10 Hz beat, so the harness would falsely report the beat test as insensitive at every overlap. Confirm cutoff is none or <=3 Hz and remove onset/offset shape with a LOW-ORDER polynomial (or Model-A reconstruction), not a high-pass.

CHIRPLET count-vs-geometry confusion (anti-bias c): scoring 'dual' as 'nAtoms>=2' will mislabel the singleNL family (which legitimately needs 2-3 linked atoms) as dual, faking a specificity failure. Score on trajectory CONNECTIVITY (centers chain end-to-end, chirp signs consistent), and use Neff=#cycles for any BIC, never raw sample count (raw-N BIC is wildly overconfident on autocorrelated oscillatory residuals).

mle_adapt_chirplets EM bug (KEY API FACT): do not call it; use mp_adapt_chirplets / mp_act_signal. Q=0 silently calls ginput and HANGS a headless/WMI-detached MATLAB; always pass Q>0 and verbose='no'.

FASLT output is POWER, not analytic (KEY API FACT): phase and envelope for the phase/beat tests must come from hilbert() of the 25-58 FIR-bandpassed signal, never from nfaslt. The harness must build the analytic signal the same way the real pipeline does, or it validates the wrong estimator.

EDGE EFFECTS: synth padMs too small -> FASLT/FIR border artifacts at window edges inflate ridge RMSE and fake phase dispersion. Pad >= longest wavelet half-support + FIR group delay, then trim to [-1,+3] s before any test reads the window — mirror Phase-1 exactly.

UNDECIDABLE not reported (spec 0.2/0.5/e): the dualLocked degenerate family and short-overlap/small-Df cells WILL be inconclusive for every test; the harness must label these cells 'undecidable/no-teeth' rather than forcing a single/dual call, and these cells define the regime where real-data verdicts must read 'undecidable'.

WINDOW-FINDING vs TEST error conflation: if the harness only feeds ridge-derived windows, a ridge failure looks like a test failure. Score each test twice — with ground-truth coexistWin/transitionWin (oracle window) AND with the pipeline-derived window — so the deliverables separate estimator error from window error.

SNR mismatch: defining SNR broadband instead of in-band (25-58 Hz) makes the synthetic noise floor wrong and the sensitivity tables non-transferable. Define SNR after the FIR, and source it from measure_burst_lengths on real trials, not a guess.

SINGLE-family ampRatio double-counting: single families have one component; sweeping them over ampRatioGrid would triple-count identical trials and bias the aggregate. Fix ampRatio=NaN for single families and de-duplicate in scoring.
designs.mapsToHypothesis: "The harness produces NO single/dual verdict on real data — it produces the LICENSE to interpret Phase-1 on real data. A positive result = a (test, overlap, Df, ampRatio) cell where sensitivity>=0.8 AND specificity>=0.8: in that regime the test's positive call is trustworthy (beat firing -> reads as evidence FOR dual; phase residual concentrated -> reads as evidence FOR single). A null/failure cell = the test has no teeth there, so on real trials whose measured overlap/Df fall in that cell the test contributes 'inconclusive', NEVER a default to single or dual. The min-coexistence table cross-referenced with the real burst/overlap distribution (measure_burst_lengths) decides, per test, whether the real regime is one where that test can speak at all; where the real overlap sits below every test's minimum (or in the dualLocked-like degenerate zone), the regime itself is marked UNDECIDABLE and Phase-3 must report undecidable. Concretely: confirming the beat-minimum-overlap recovery and the disappearance of the chirplet single-bias once overlap>>1/Df is what permits reading a real beat as dual and a real single-trajectory as single; failing to confirm them voids those reads."
outputs: phase0_results.mat (-v7.3): full results struct {sweepCfg, perCell test outcomes, ground truth, sensitivity/specificity tables, all curves, real-data calibration used} — the auditable record gating interpretation.

phase0_sensitivity.csv: one row per (test, family, overlapMs, Df, ampRatio) with sensitivity, specificity, nTrials, positiveCallRate — maps directly onto spec 7.x asymmetric-test reading and the 0.2 verdict logic.

beat_min_overlap.csv + curve PNG: minimum overlapMs for >=2 detected beat cycles & modSNR>surrogate, per Df (x ampRatio) — spec 5 deliverable 2; gates which real sessions the beat test may speak on (Phase-3 §8 beat gate).

chirplet_bias.csv + curve PNG: fraction-classified-single on true-dual vs overlap (must drop past 1/Df) and singleNL one-connected-trajectory fraction with nAtomsSig distribution — spec 5 deliverable 3 (geometry-not-count proof).

phase_segmentation.csv + panel PNG: segmented vs unsegmented meanRbar on single families, and slip-localization-at-beat-nulls metric on dual — spec 5 deliverable 4 (validates the 150 ms sub-window correction).

min_coexistence.csv + real-burst overlay PNG: per-test minimum coexistence for sens&spec>=0.8, overlaid on the real burst/overlap-length distribution — spec 5 deliverable 5; the number that bounds the project and flags the undecidable regime.
