Console/log assertions: hard checks that ifSource=='ridgePower' (not dphi/dt), beat HP cutoff<=3 Hz or none, chirplet Q>0 & verbose='no' & Neff='cycles' — fail loud (spec: prefer strict over flexible) so an anti-bias violation cannot silently pass.

risks.component: chirp_tfr_faslt vs all consumers — pad/trim contract
risks.risk: nfaslt does its OWN internal zero-padding (computed from the largest wavelet half-support at 20 Hz, ~hundreds of samples) and returns [Nf x Npoints] at the SAME length as input via 'same' convolution. The designs ALSO require an upstream epoch pad ('pad beyond [-1,+3]s then trim trimSamp'). If chirp_tfr_faslt trims trimSamp off the FASLT output assuming the epoch pad is the only edge protection, the two pads are conflated: trimSamp is the EPOCH pad (chosen so [-1,3] is clean), but nfaslt's internal pad already absorbs wavelet edge effects within the supplied buffer. The real risk is the REVERSE: the spec's ~600ms epoch pad must be >= the longest wavelet half-support at flo=20Hz (with c1=3 the 20Hz Morlet half-support at 2.5 SD is ~3*0.5*(1/20)/2.5*... ≈ hundreds of ms), or the ridge band 25-58 still sees curvature/taper at the trim boundary. Per nfaslt cxmorlet: wl ≈ 6*sd*Fs samples, sd=(Nc/2)/Fc/2.5; at 25 Hz with order up to 30 (Nc=90), sd≈0.72s, half-support ≈2.16s — FAR exceeds padMs=600. The high-order superlets at the LOW end of the ridge band have multi-second support; a 600ms pad is insufficient and the ridge near transition onset will be biased by edge taper.
risks.fix: Set epoch padMs from the ACTUAL max wavelet half-support: compute max over the bank of fix(numel(wavelet)/2)/fs after building the cache, and require padMs >= that (likely ~2.2 s at 25 Hz / order 30, not 600 ms). Either raise padMs to ~2.5 s or cap the adaptive order at the low ridge-band edge (e.g. olo→ohi schedule so 25 Hz uses order ~3-8, not 30). Document that nfaslt's internal pad protects the SUPPLIED buffer but the analyst-facing [-1,3] window still needs the epoch pad >= wavelet half-support. Verify in Phase 0 that ridgePower at tStart is flat for a pure tone.

risks.component: chirp_ridge anchors vs chirp_phase_test transition window (integration mismatch)
risks.risk: chirp_ridge derives transitionWin PER TRIAL from each trial's noisy single-trial ridge (movmedian smoothing of fhat, crossing f_hi-1Hz to f_lo+1Hz). chirp_ridge_anchors derives f_hi/f_lo ONCE from the subject-average meanPower ridge, clamped [27,56], and explicitly INWARD-biased by onset jitter. The phase test consumes BOTH a per-trial transWin AND (via cfg) the subject-average f_hi/f_lo. If the inward-biased average anchors are used to DEFINE per-trial crossing times (tStart=first time fhat<f_hi-1), then on a trial whose true f_hi exceeds the inward-biased average f_hi, tStart is set too late (or never triggers) and the transition window is truncated or empty — biasing the phase test toward FEWER sub-windows on exactly the high-amplitude trials, and silently dropping trials (included=false, reason=tooShort). This couples anchor bias into per-trial inclusion, an uncontrolled selection effect.
risks.fix: Decouple: derive each trial's transitionWin SOLELY from that trial's own smoothed fhat extrema (its own max/plateau), NOT from the subject-average anchors. Reserve the clamped average f_hi/f_lo for the THREE uses the spec lists (phase crossing-time ANNOTATION, spatial band centers, figure labels) — never as the per-trial window gate. Add an explicit assert that transitionWin derivation does not read cfg.f_hi/f_lo.

risks.component: chirp_phase_test ifSource guard — necessary but insufficient
risks.risk: The ifSource=='ridgePower' literal assert prevents the obvious dphi/dt wiring, but a subtler vacuity remains: the PRIMARY ridge fhat is the MAX-energy path of the SAME broadband signal whose Hilbert phase is phiObs. For a clean single oscillator these are near-identical by construction, so a concentrated residual is partly tautological — the test's POWER to discriminate comes only from cases where the ridge and the broadband phase DIVERGE (i.e., true dual / beating). The asymmetric reading (concentrated=single) is therefore only meaningful relative to the permutation null, AND only if the ridge is not itself a smoothed copy of dphi/dt. With NumFrequencyBins~2 and penalty~1, the ridge IS a smoothed energy path, which is acceptable, but the Phase-0 harness MUST verify on dualIndep trials that the residual actually DISPERSES (specificity), not just that singleLin concentrates (sensitivity). If specificity on dualIndep is not demonstrated, the test is vacuous in the discriminating direction even with the guard.
risks.fix: In Phase 0, score chirp_phase_test on dualIndep AND dualLocked families and REQUIRE specificity>=0.8 (residual dispersed, perm_z~0) before the phase test may contribute 'single' to any real verdict. Document perm_z's null is the rotation of WITHIN-trial residual structure — confirm the rotation preserves the per-trial subWinResid vector length so n-dependence is truly absorbed. Treat phase-test 'single' as licensed ONLY in (overlap,Df) cells where Phase-0 specificity passed.

risks.component: chirp_beat_test / chirp_temporal_decoup / chirp_spatial — power-vs-amplitude envelope inconsistency
risks.risk: The beat test builds env=abs(hilbert(bb)) — an AMPLITUDE envelope. The temporal-decoupling and spatial tests build band-limited envelopes by integrating FASLT POWER over [fHi±band]/[fLo±band]. A beat at fBeat=|f_hi-f_lo| appears at fBeat in the AMPLITUDE envelope but at fBeat (and 2*fBeat from the squaring) in the POWER envelope, and modIndex/modSNR scales differ (power roughly doubles the modulation depth and shifts spectral content). If decoupling/spatial latency peaks are read off POWER envelopes while beat is read off AMPLITUDE, the three tests are not on a common footing and Phase-0 calibration of one does not transfer to the others. Worse, the band-limited POWER envelope at fHi from FASLT is geometric-mean-pooled across superlet orders — it is NOT a clean linear power and its AM depth is distorted, contradicting the KEY API FACT that envelope must come from hilbert() of the bandpassed signal.
risks.fix: Standardize: derive ALL envelopes (beat, decoupling band-limited, spatial band powers) from hilbert() of NARROW FIR-bandpassed signals (broadband 25-58 for beat; [fHi-band,fHi+band] and [fLo-band,fLo+band] FIR for the band-limited ones), squaring to power only where 'power' is explicitly wanted and documenting amplitude-vs-power per test. Do NOT take band-limited envelopes from FASLT power for the latency/spatial peaks. Reserve FASLT power strictly for the spectrogram display (6.3), ridge tracking, and ridge-power statistics. Add one cfg.envDomain field ('amplitude'|'power') recorded per test so Phase-0 sensitivity tables are interpretable.

risks.risk: chirp_spatial requires goodMac (QC mask over macBP), contactGeom (numeric pair-position/spacing), and an 'on-bulb' filter to count nGoodContacts. But the codebase selects the OB channel via FOOOF gamma-peak ('bestMac' in cue_fooof_macBP.m), NOT via chanType or any bulb-location/geometry table — and the spec itself lists 'OB contact identification idiom' and 'contact geometry/spacing' as UNCONFIRMED open items. There is currently NO source for contactGeom or an on-bulb membership test. As designed, chirp_spatial cannot compute its eligibility gate or the bipolar-spacing caveat, so it will either error or silently treat all macBP as on-bulb/adequately-spaced — collapsing the 'not assessed' vs 'matched' distinction that spec 8.1 makes load-bearing.
risks.fix: Block the spatial build behind resolving the OB-contact/geometry source FIRST (it is a stated user-confirm item). Until contactGeom exists, chirp_spatial must set eligible=false with reason='geometryUnknown' for ALL sessions (never default to eligible), so the group step correctly reads 'spatial: not assessed' everywhere rather than fabricating matched profiles. Single-channel battery (which carries the no-spatial participants per spec §4) must be fully functional without it. Add nGoodContacts/contactSpacing as first-class outputs even when geometryUnknown.

risks.component: chirp_beat_test surrogates vs chirp_ridge surrogates vs chirplet surrogates — cost and consistency
risks.risk: Three independent surrogate procedures (ridge-2 energy, beat modSNR, chirplet atom energy) each generate 200-1000 per-trial FFT phase-randomized surrogates and push them through FASLT (ridge) or fits (chirplet). With 40 cue trials x ~35 sessions x 3 procedures x up to 1000 surrogates x FASLT kernel rebuild, this is the batch bottleneck; if any procedure forgets the kernel cache (component-1 flags this only for ridge) the runtime is multiplied. Also: the THREE surrogate sets must use the SAME phase-randomization recipe (preserve magnitude spectrum, enforce conjugate symmetry → real, re-hilbert for analytic consumers) or their 95th-percentile thresholds are not mutually comparable, and a trial deemed beat-significant under one recipe but ridge-insignificant under another produces an incoherent verdict vector.
risks.fix: Single shared surrogate generator chirp_surrogates(bb, nSurr, rngSeed) returning the real phase-randomized time series; each test re-hilberts/re-FASLTs as needed but draws from the SAME surrogate signals per trial (same rngSeed → identical surrogate set across tests for a given trial). Share the cached FASLT kernel bank (keyed on fs,flo,fhi,Nf,c1,olo,ohi,mult) across ridge AND any FASLT-based surrogate path. Fix nSurr=200 for the batch, 1000 only for the one profiled Phase-0 session, recorded in cfg.

risks.component: chirp_chirplet analytic-input reconstruction for errA/errB BIC
risks.risk: The fit feeds hilbert(crop) (analytic, complex) to mp_adapt_chirplets and reconstructs with make_chirplets(N,P,'PeriodEff',true). errA=norm(x-xA)^2 with x analytic. But the Neff=#gamma cycles BIC and the dBIC sign depend on errA/errB being on the analytic signal consistently — and make_chirplets default PeriodEff=true periodizes with rep=5 and unit-normalizes each atom, while em_chirplets (the fit) ALSO uses PeriodEff=true (confirmed). The risk is the dBIC structural test is only LICENSED where Phase-0 says so, yet the design computes it unconditionally; on a true-single nonlinear sweep forced into Model-B (2 flat atoms), errB can be spuriously low (2 atoms fit anything better) and dBIC>0 even though geometry says single. dBIC is a count-flavored statistic sneaking back in.
risks.fix: Compute dBIC but GATE its interpretation exactly as spec 6.7 says ('only as corroboration', 'where Phase 0 licenses it'). The PRIMARY chirplet output must be trajConnectivity/classification (geometry), and the driver must NOT let dBIC override a 'single' geometry call. In Phase 0, verify on singleNL that dBIC does NOT favor Model-B (specificity); if it does at the real overlap regime, drop dBIC from the verdict entirely. Confirm errA/errB both computed on the analytic x with identical PeriodEff=true.

risks.component: Phase-0 harness ground-truth window vs pipeline-derived window scoring
risks.risk: If the harness feeds only ridge-derived transition/coexistence windows to the tests, a ridge-extraction failure (penalty mis-calibration, edge bias) is indistinguishable from a test failure, and the min-coexistence table that BOUNDS the whole project will be pessimistic for the wrong reason. Component-5 names this but the per-test scoring tables (phase0_sensitivity.csv keyed on test x cell x family) do not obviously carry the oracle-vs-derived axis.
risks.fix: Add a windowSource column ('oracle'|'pipeline') to phase0_sensitivity.csv and run every test TWICE per trial (ground-truth coexistWin/transitionWin from gt, and pipeline-derived). Report both surfaces; the gap is the window-finding error budget. The project-bounding min-coexistence number must be reported for BOTH so the user sees whether ridge tracking or the test itself is the limiter.

risks.component: chirp_ridge powerDipStat flank definition vs transition window
risks.risk: powerDipStat = min(ridgePower in transitionWin) / mean(flanking maxima). Flanks are ~150ms windows just before tStart and after tEnd. But tStart/tEnd are derived from fhat crossings, and the PRE-transition flank (before tStart) may fall in the pre-onset BASELINE where gamma is absent → flank max ~0 → ratio explodes → false 'no dip' (reads single) OR div-by-0. Component-1 flags the div-by-0 but the deeper issue is the pre-transition flank for a sniff-locked burst that RISES at onset has no high-gamma plateau before the descent begins, so a genuine sequential handover's dip cannot be normalized against a pre-flank that never had power.
risks.fix: Define flanks RELATIVE TO THE BURST ENVELOPE, not the transition crossings: pre-flank = the first ~150ms where ridgePower exceeds a burst-present threshold (post-onset gamma rise), post-flank = last ~150ms still above threshold before burst decay. Guard: if either flank max < burstThreshold, set powerDipStat=NaN and mark not-included for the dip read (do NOT let it read as single). Validate the statistic only on Phase-0 dualIndep (true handover) vs singleLin (no dip).

risks.component: Cross-component transition vs coexistence window naming
risks.risk: Phase and chirplet use transitionWin (frequency-changing span, excludes stationary tail). Beat uses coexistWin (full two-component overlap span). chirp_ridge outputs transitionWin per trial and a separate coexistWin; chirp_temporal_decoup finds latencies 'within the transition window'; chirp_spatial uses earlyWin/lateWin at 20th/80th transition percentiles. If any consumer silently substitutes one window for the other (e.g. beat reads transitionWin instead of coexistWin), it will undercount beat cycles in a long overlap with a stationary tail → biases beat toward 'not enough cycles' → inconclusive → unwarranted lean to single. The two windows are genuinely different and must both be plumbed.
risks.fix: chirp_ridge must emit BOTH transitionWin and coexistWin per trial as named fields; every downstream function takes its window as an explicit named argument (transWin vs coexistWin) — never a generic 'win'. Add asserts that beat receives coexistWin and phase/chirplet receive transitionWin. Document in the unified config which test consumes which.

risks.component: chirp_phase_test slip-vs-beat-null cross-reference creates a hidden p-value coupling
risks.risk: The phase test records whether slips coincide with chirp_beating's beatNullTimes and treats coincidence as 'leans dual'. This reuses the beat test's output INSIDE the phase test, so the two tests are no longer independent views — and if a downstream verdict counts both 'beat present' AND 'phase slips at beat nulls' as separate dual evidence, that is exactly the p-value multiplication spec 0.2 forbids (same data, same beat structure, counted twice).
risks.fix: Keep slip-at-null tagging as a DESCRIPTIVE annotation only (for figures / localization), explicitly NOT a separate verdict-vector element. The verdict vector gets ONE beat element and ONE phase element; slip-localization may corroborate a beat call qualitatively but must not add an independent dual vote. Document this in the convergence-logic so the group script does not double-count.

risks.component: chirp_chirplet [22 62] Hz atom band-filter vs ridge band 25-58
risks.risk: Atoms are filtered to fc in [22,62] Hz, wider than the 25-58 ridge/filter band. Since seg is FIR-bandpassed 25-58 before hilbert, no real signal energy exists at 22-25 or 58-62, so atoms there are fit artifacts/edge leakage. Keeping them (22-62) admits skirt-band artifact atoms into the trajectory-geometry read, potentially creating spurious 'parallel' edges near the band edges that bias toward dual.
risks.fix: Tighten the atom-keep band to match the analysis band where signal actually lives (e.g. [25,58] or a hair inside, [26,57]) so no atom can be placed in the FIR transition skirt. If a margin is wanted for fit slop, make it small (±1 Hz) and document that no real energy exists beyond 25-58.

critic.sharedSubstrateNotes: All five components must agree on a SINGLE shared cfg struct and three shared data objects, plus one task-shared / task-specific split mirroring the existing pipeline. (1) CONFIG: one chirpCfg struct built once per run (setup_chirpAnalysis_paths.m registers Superlets/MPACT/mpact paths for both machines; labPaths block adds GitHub roots). Every function takes cfg and reads its params by name — no function hard-codes fs, bands, or windows. The unifiedConfig table above is that struct. (2) EPOCH TENSOR: epochs are built ONCE per channel as a real [nSamp x nTrial] matrix around behDat.finalOnset (behDat is a TABLE, index by name; cueTask sniffLabel=='cued' & wiTriali==1; O15 selected sniff config, truncate at next finalOnset → burstTruncated). The PADDED tensor (padMs derived from the actual max FASLT wavelet half-support, NOT 600 ms) is the shared substrate; trimSamp/trimming is applied consistently downstream. Channels selected by contains(label,'macBP') and bestMac (FOOOF gamma-peak, as in cue_fooof_macBP.m) — never row index; rows 1-32 EEG excluded from spatial. (3) CACHED TFR: chirp_tfr_faslt produces the FASLT POWER tensor [Nf x nT x nTrial] + meanPower ONCE per channel, with the wavelet bank memoized (persistent, keyed on fs,flo,fhi,Nf,c1,olo,ohi,mult). This single TFR is consumed by ridge (6.4), spectrogram display (6.3), and is the ONLY licensed use of FASLT power. CRITICAL: phase/envelope for beat/phase/decoup/spatial come from hilbert() of FIR-bandpassed signal, NEVER from this power TFR (KEY API FACT). (4) SHARED WINDOWS: chirp_ridge emits per-trial transitionWin AND coexistWin AND the anchors; downstream functions receive the correct window by explicit named arg (phase/chirplet←transitionWin, beat←coexistWin, spatial early/late←transition percentiles). (5) SHARED SURROGATES: one chirp_surrogates(bb,nSurr,rngSeed) generator feeds ridge-2, beat, and chirplet so their 95th-pctile thresholds are mutually comparable; phase uses a DIFFERENT (rotation) null and emits no surrogate p. Verdict vector has ONE element per test (phase, beat, spatial, decoup, chirplet) — slip-at-null and dBIC are corroborative annotations, not extra votes (no p-value multiplication, spec 0.2).
critic.goAhead: Conditional go. Build order: (0) setup_chirpAnalysis_paths.m + the unified chirpCfg struct + measure_burst_lengths.m on a few real O15/cue sessions FIRST — this sets padMs (from real burst length AND the FASLT wavelet half-support, which the 600 ms default badly underestimates) and snrDb, and surfaces the OB-contact/geometry open item. (1) chirp_tfr_faslt with kernel cache + chirp_ridge (primary, peeling, anchors, transition/coexist windows, dip stat) — the substrate everything else needs; calibrate tfridge penalty here. (2) chirp_phase0_harness + chirp_synth_trial, scoring on BOTH oracle and pipeline windows; this GATES interpretation, so it must precede any real-data verdict. (3) chirp_phase_test (primary single-channel test) and chirp_chirplet (geometry) in parallel — both consume transitionWin. (4) chirp_beat_test + chirp_temporal_decoup (consume coexistWin / band envelopes from FIR-hilbert). (5) chirp_spatial LAST and only after the OB-contact geometry source is confirmed (block as eligible=false='geometryUnknown' until then; the single-channel battery must stand alone per spec §4). (6) run_chirp_analysis_pipeline.m driver + CSVs + group adjudication. Hard blockers before real-data conclusions: padMs must cover the actual wavelet support (high); per-trial transitionWin must NOT be gated by the inward-biased average anchors (high); all envelopes from FIR-hilbert not FASLT power (high); spatial eligibility cannot default to true without a real geometry source (high). Profile ONE session locally, then run the chirplet+surrogate batch on labdesktop (parfor, outputs to E:).
